correctness.rationale: Proof reconstructed for every labeled simple cycle n>=5. Under the graph definitions, D domination iff no cyclic 111, L domination iff no cyclic 000. For n>=5 distinct zero vertices can share a nonempty L-neighborhood iff they are distance two, have one shared L neighbor and their two other neighbors both belong to D, i.e. a cyclic 00100; the special n=4 obstruction is excluded. Alternating runs have lengths 1 or 2; forbidding transition (a,b,a_next)=(2,1,2) yields the stated exact two-state transfer. Cyclic marking gives n/k even for nonprimitive periodic words. det(I-T)=1-u z²-u²(z³+z⁴+z⁵)-u³z⁶, giving exact rational derivative; subtract formal small n=2,3,4 terms. Coefficient recurrence holds n>=11 after boundary correction. Independent direct graph brute versus pattern checker and algebraic polynomial engine agree for every 5<=n<=17; all computations reproducible. Finite checks alone do not prove the unrestricted result.

originality.rationale: The novel assessed object is the full vertex-cardinality-refined polynomial for typed domination/locating-domination cycle partitions and its exact binary-word classification. Chakraborty et al. (2026) prove existence and a polynomial algorithm for arbitrary isolate-free graphs (Theorem 6, Section 3) but do not enumerate all partitions or refine by |L|. Foucaud et al. treat two locating-dominating classes, not the typed D/L statistic. Chellali et al. treat coalition partitions in which *no* block is locating-dominating, the logical opposite of the requirement on L here. OEIS A001636 contains the univariate total sequence and an already-published rational generating function; this portion is explicitly conceded as previously known and is not the asserted novel contribution. Neither that generic integer sequence nor its recurrence records the graph interpretation or distribution of |L|. No equivalent bivariate graph-class result was encountered in the inspected primary texts or semantic searches; unindexed broader combinatorial transfer results remain a genuine risk. The coalition paper already uses classical no-consecutive-two-gaps constraints for LD sets of cycles; no novelty is claimed for that local fact alone.
residual_risks: Full earlier graph enumeration of these same typed partitions may exist under unsearched terminology or in inaccessible/unindexed literature.
The univariate sequence, denominator and conventional transfer-matrix method are known; originality is limited to the cycle DLDS interpretation and new bivariate refinement.
The 2025 two-LD-set article was reviewed in HTML rather than an independently typeset PDF; an overlooked appendix or later revision cannot be ruled out.

value.rationale: New 2026 general theorem assures a typed D/LD partition exists for every isolate-free graph but does not quantify possible choices. The cycle size distribution is a complete natural infinite-family classification, tracking the locating-set cardinality central to the definition. The three exact forbidden local obstructions give a structural code for every valid partition; the bivariate rational expression gives each coefficient for arbitrary n and a size-recursive enumerator. The 1973 Fielder univariate sequence happens to coincide, but its coefficients cannot recover the graph interpretation or cardinality-refined distribution. The bounded extra variable is motivated by the graph invariant rather than an arbitrary slice.
